title: adaptive-staleness-rollback-and-routing-for-quantized-kernels
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Background and motivation: During surge traffic on a customer dedicated cluster we observed repeated correctness rollbacks caused by stale KV-cache entries combined with optimistic kernel selection for 4-bit quantized paths. Those rollbacks lead to tail-latency spikes and client retries. This PR implements an adaptive staleness detector + rollback routing layer that reduces unnecessary kernel swaps while preserving a strict correctness fallback when mismatches are detected.

What this change does: Adds a low-overhead staleness score computed from sequence-level KV hits, token-level cache age, and recent kernel-compatibility probe results. When the score exceeds a configurable threshold the request is routed to a conservative path (higher-precision kernel or a locked KV-consistency path). Instead of immediately switching kernels for a tenant, we now do a short-lived staging period that validates a sampled subset of requests on the conservative path while keeping most traffic on the optimized quantized runtime. If the staged checks fail, we perform a per-tenant rollback and emit a detailed incident metric.

Key design notes: - Staleness score is exponential-moving-average based to avoid reacting to single outliers. - Sampling uses deterministic request hashing per-tenant to ensure reproducible validation and low variance. - The conservative path uses existing 8-bit kernels (no new kernel code) and a strictly consistent KV fetch mode (wait-for-parent when necessary). - All thresholds are configurable through runtime flags (runtime.staleness.{threshold,decay,sample_rate}).

Testing and verification: Unit tests cover score calculation and routing decisions. Integration harness runs with benchmark-lab compositions to validate no correctness regressions. Added a synthetic failure injector test that simulates stale cache entries and asserts rollback occurs within the staging window.

Checklist: - [x] Implement staleness estimator and routing gates - [x] Add sampling + staging logic - [x] Add metrics and tracing hooks - [x] Integration tests in benchmark-lab config - [x] Documentation snippet in runtime/README (config flags) - [x] Manual smoke test on internal dedicated cluster

Related: ENG-6122 is the original investigation ticket. SUP-1347 is the customer incident that prompted the fix.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the sampling determinism and the default threshold (set conservatively). This is intentionally conservative in behavior by default; we can tune thresholds separately in follow-ups for edge workloads.

review_thread: Evan Chu: Could you explain why we chose an EMA instead of simple windowed counts? Concerned about reaction time on bursty workloads.

Aisha Patel: EMA gives us tunable memory vs reaction; with decay=0.8 we still react within ~5 tokens in practice. We experimented with windowed counts and saw noisier toggles in synthetic bursts (benchmarks in the branch).
Maria Gonzales: Add telemetry for per-tenant staging failures so we can run dashboard-driven rollbacks later.
Aisha Patel: Added metrics: staleness_score, staging_validation_pass, staging_validation_fail and a per-tenant rollback counter.

performance_summary: Microbenchmarks: steady-state throughput for quantized kernels unchanged (+0.5%) when staging enabled; sampled validation added 2% CPU overhead at 2% sample rate. Fault scenario: when we inject stale KV entries, end-to-end client retries reduced by 78% and 95th percentile latency improved by up to 420ms compared to blind kernel switch rollback. Overall tradeoff: small steady-state cost for large reduction in correctness-driven tail events.
release_notes: Add adaptive staleness detection and conservative rollback routing to reduce correctness-induced rollbacks; defaults conservative to avoid user-visible regressions; flags available to tune thresholds and sample rates.
